title: Dressing Children for a Winter Wedding
meta_description: Pakistani wedding season is the coldest part of the year and most functions are outdoors after dark. How to keep a child warm without ruining the outfit.
keywords: kids winter wedding outfit Pakistan, warm formal wear children, girls winter shaadi dress, velvet kids outfit Pakistan, children outdoor wedding cold
excerpt: A child at an outdoor December wedding is colder than you are, complains sooner, and ends the evening in someone's shawl. This is how to avoid it.
imagePrompt: A child's deep emerald velvet frock with fine gold embroidery laid flat on cream linen, beside a folded soft woollen shawl, warm tights, closed embroidered flat shoes and a small pair of gold earrings. Dried marigold and a brass lantern softly out of focus behind. Warm low evening light, shallow depth of field, rich winter editorial still life, no faces, no text.

content.content:
Wedding season in Pakistan runs from November to February, which is the coldest stretch of the year, and most functions are held outdoors on a lawn or under a marquee, starting at nine at night.

Adults manage this badly. Children manage it worse, and for a specific reason: they lose heat faster than adults do because they have more surface area relative to their size, and they will not tell you they are cold until they are miserable.

The usual outcome is a beautiful outfit under a borrowed shawl by half past ten, and a child who wants to go home. It is avoidable, but it has to be planned into the outfit rather than added on top at the door.

content.heading: Be Honest About the Temperature
content.content:
Lahore and Islamabad drop to around 4–8°C on a December or January night, and lower in the north. Karachi is milder but a sea breeze after midnight is colder than the forecast reads.

A marquee is not warm. The sides are usually open and the heaters warm a radius of about two metres, which is where the adults are standing.

And the timing works against a child more than an adult. You arrive at nine, when it is merely cool. The function runs to one in the morning. In between, a small child will alternate between running around — and getting hot and sweaty — and sitting still, which is when the cold arrives properly.

That cycle is the actual problem. Dressing for it means layers that can come off when she is running and go back on when she sits, not one warm garment that is either right or wrong.

content.heading: Fabrics That Are Warm and Look Right
content.content:
**Velvet** is the winter children's formal fabric and it genuinely earns its place. Warm, rich under low lighting, and a velvet frock or kurta needs very little embellishment to look finished. Deep tones — emerald, wine, navy, plum — photograph beautifully under warm string lights.

**Raw silk** is warmer than it appears. It has body and blocks wind far better than chiffon, and it holds a clean shape in cold air.

**Jamawar and brocade** are woven heavy by nature and give texture without embroidery.

**Khaddar** is the practical semi-formal choice for dholkis and smaller functions.

**Wool-blend** kurtas and frocks are increasingly available and are the most comfortable of all for a child, though less formal.

What not to put a child in outdoors in January: unlined chiffon, organza, net and thin georgette. All four give no protection from wind at all, and a net frock with a stiff underskirt is both cold and scratchy. Our [seasonal fabric guide](/journal/summer-vs-winter-fabric-guide-pakistani-women) covers how these behave, and the [fabric glossary](/content/fabric-glossary) explains the labels.

content.heading: Lining and Layers Underneath
content.content:
Lining does more than the outer fabric, and it is the thing to ask about when buying.

A fully lined frock is dramatically warmer than an unlined one in the same fabric, because the trapped air between the two layers is what insulates. Many children's formal pieces are lined only through the bodice, leaving the sleeves and skirt open — ask specifically.

**A cotton lining is comfortable but not warm. A silk or satin lining is warmer** and slides over layers underneath, which matters if she is wearing thermals.

**Thin thermal tops** under a full-sleeved kurta are invisible and change everything. Choose one close to her skin tone if there is any chance of it showing at the neck or wrist — white under ivory is fine, black under ivory is not.

**Warm tights or fleece-lined leggings** under a frock or shalwar. Legs are where children lose most heat at a lawn function and the part most often left bare.

**Avoid bulk at the shoulder.** A thick layer under a fitted bodice changes the fit and reads immediately as padding.

content.heading: Feet, Which Are the Real Problem
content.content:
She will be on grass, on marquee carpet laid straight over a lawn, or on a marble floor. All three are colder than they look, and cold feet end a child's evening faster than anything else.

**Closed shoes.** Winter is the one season when closed shoes are clearly better than khussas or open sandals for children. Velvet or embroidered closed flats are widely available.

**Warm socks or thick tights**, in a colour that works if they show.

**Not a new pair.** Cold makes shoes stiffer, and a wedding is hours of standing and running. Break them in over a few evenings first.

**Something she can put on herself.** At a home function shoes come off at the door, and a child who cannot manage her own buckles will need you every time.

**Pack a spare pair of socks.** Grass is damp at a winter lawn function and wet socks are the fastest route to a miserable child.

Our [festive wear guide](/journal/kids-festive-wear-guide-pakistani-weddings) maps what suits each function across the wedding week.

content.heading: The Shawl and the Outer Layer
content.content:
Plan the outer layer as part of the outfit, not as something grabbed on the way out.

**A soft woollen or pashmina shawl** in a plain neutral works over almost any formal outfit and can be wrapped properly rather than draped decoratively.

**A tailored waistcoat or a short embroidered jacket** is better than a shawl for a younger child, because it stays on. A shawl on a six-year-old lasts about ten minutes.

**A cardigan in a matching or neutral tone** is unglamorous and genuinely the most practical option for a small child. Nobody will mind.

**Avoid a bulky coat over a formal outfit** — it crushes the shape and she will refuse to wear it for photographs, which is exactly when you want it on.

The practical point: whatever the outer layer is, she needs to be able to take it off and put it back on herself, because she will do this eight times across the evening and you will not be there for all of them.

content.heading: Comfort Decides Whether She Keeps It On
content.content:
The best winter outfit is the one she does not fight.

**Check the inside seams and the lining.** Scratchy net linings, exposed embroidery backing and stiff zari on the inside of a sleeve are the commonest reasons a child pulls at an outfit all evening.

**Avoid heavy embroidery across the shoulders and back.** It is where the weight sits and where she notices it.

**Avoid a stiff net underskirt.** Cold, scratchy, and it stops her sitting comfortably.

**Sleeve length matters.** Full sleeves for winter, but not so long they cover her hands while she eats.

**Test it before the day.** An hour at home in the full outfit — sitting, standing, arms up — tells you everything. It is far better to discover a problem three days early than at the venue.

Our [quality checklist](/journal/quality-kids-festive-outfit-mothers-buying-checklist) covers what to inspect before buying, and the [care guide](/journal/care-for-kids-embroidered-outfits-washing-storage) covers keeping it wearable afterwards.

content.heading: The Bag to Bring
content.content:
A winter wedding runs late, and a prepared parent has a much easier night.

**A change of clothes** for anyone under about seven. Something will be spilled, and a simple spare kurta turns a ruined evening into a five-minute interruption.

**Spare socks**, for the damp grass problem.

**The cardigan or shawl**, even if she is refusing it at eight o'clock. She will want it at midnight.

**A hair tie.** Whatever was done to her hair will not survive the evening.

**Something to eat.** Dinner at a Pakistani wedding is served late, and a hungry cold child at eleven is a different proposition from a fed one.

One last point on choosing the outfit at all: buy something she can wear again. Winter formal wear in a good fabric works across a whole season of functions and for Eid, and children outgrow things faster than they wear them out. The [girls formal](/kids/girls-formal) section and the wider [kids collection](/kids) are cut with that in mind, and our [sizing guide for children](/journal/how-to-pick-right-festive-outfit-size-child-pakistan) covers buying with a little room to grow.

questions.question: What is the warmest formal fabric for a child in winter?
questions.answer: Velvet, followed by jamawar, brocade and raw silk. All four are warm enough for an outdoor evening function and formal enough for a wedding. Avoid unlined chiffon, organza and net outdoors after dark — they give no wind protection, and stiff net is cold and scratchy as well.

questions.question: How do I keep a child warm at an outdoor wedding without ruining the outfit?
questions.answer: Ask for a full lining rather than a bodice-only lining, add a thin thermal top under a full-sleeved kurta, put her in warm tights or fleece-lined leggings, and choose closed shoes with thick socks. Layering underneath works far better than adding bulk on top.

questions.question: Should children wear closed shoes to a winter wedding?
questions.answer: Yes. Grass, marquee carpet laid over a lawn and marble floors are all much colder than they look, and cold feet end a child's evening faster than anything else. Closed embroidered or velvet flats with warm socks, broken in over a few evenings beforehand.

questions.question: Is a shawl practical for a small child?
questions.answer: Not really — a shawl on a young child stays on for about ten minutes. A short embroidered jacket, a tailored waistcoat or even a plain matching cardigan stays put and she can manage it herself, which matters because she will take it off and put it back on repeatedly.

questions.question: Why does my child pull at her formal outfit all evening?
questions.answer: Usually the inside rather than the outside — scratchy net lining, exposed embroidery backing on the inner sleeve, or a stiff net underskirt. Check the seams and lining before buying, and have her wear the full outfit at home for an hour before the day.
